**Merge joins, rebase rewrites.**

A merge makes one new commit with two parents. Both histories stay exactly as they were.

A rebase copies your commits onto the tip of the other branch. The copies are new commits with new IDs, and the originals get dropped.

```mermaid
flowchart LR
  subgraph Merge
    A1[main] --> M[merge commit]
    B1[your work] --> M
  end
  subgraph Rebase
    A2[main] --> C1[copy of your work]
  end
```

Reach for rebase on your own work that nobody has pulled yet. It keeps history a straight line and makes review easier.

Reach for merge when the branch is shared, or when landing a finished feature. The merge commit records when it landed.

The one rule: never rebase commits someone else already has. Their copy and yours drift apart.
